newsitem.title: UK: SmithKline wins EU approval for Twinrix.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline wins EU approval for Twinrix.

text.p: SmithKline Beecham Plc said it has won European Union approval through a new centralised registration procedure to sell its Twinrix combined vaccine for hepatitis A and B viruses in all 15 EU countries.

"Twinrix will offer significant advantages including increased convenience for the physician and the patient, fewer injections and better compliance compared with two separate vaccination courses," the managing director of SB Biologicals said in a statement.

Priority target groups for both immunisations include "travellers to high endemicity areas, individuals at risk through their lifestyle, as well as military and exposed healthcare personnel", he added.

SmithKline said hepatitis A (HAV) and B (HBV) affect "almost every urban and rural community and are among the most common infectious diseases in the world". Both represent serious public health problems, with an estimated 1.4 million cases of HAV and 300-350 million chronic carriers of HBV, it added.
